sentences.i: I have seen a snake-charmer, expert in snakes and knowing them well, often bitten by a snake and killed; while a man who knows nothing of snakes and has no learning in their ways may get the better of one.”
sentences.n: ḥāwī, “snake-charmer”; الحاوى and الذى write ى for final ي. khabīr bi-, “expert in”: bi- marks the field of knowledge. rabbamā, “often, many a time”; the fatḥa on its rāʾ is the print's own (the word is also said rubbamā). nahashathu … fa-taqtuluhu: the telling slips from past to present. ẓafira bi-, “to get the better of”: the verb chooses bi-. معرفه, with ه for ة, and عندة, with ة for the pronoun ه, are the print's spellings, a habit of this edition; the marks on عِلْمَ are the print's own, and so is the hamza in رأيت.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَدْ خَالَفَ زَوْجَتَهُ وَاشْتَرَى الْمَتَاعَ وَأَخَذَ فِي تِلْكَ الْعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qad khālafa zawjatahu wa-ishtarā al-matāʿa wa-akhadha fī tilka al-ʿādati
sentences.l: Then he had gone-against his-wife, and bought the goods, and took-up that habit.
sentences.i: Then he went against his wife, bought the goods, and took up that practice.
sentences.n: khālafa, “to oppose, act against”. akhadha fī, “to set about, take up”. matāʿ, “goods”: the bundle he had been offered.

sentences.t: فَصَارَ يَشْتَرِي مِنَ السَّارِقِينَ بِدُونِ الْقِيمَةِ إِلَى أَنْ وَقَعَ فِي تُهْمَةٍ فَهَلَكَ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra yashtarī mina al-sāriqīna bi-dūni al-qīmati ilā an waqaʿa fī tuhmatin fa-halaka fīhā
sentences.l: And he-became buying from the thieves for below the value, until he-fell into a suspicion and perished in-it.
sentences.i: He went on buying from thieves below the true value, until he fell under suspicion and was ruined by it.
sentences.n: ṣāra yashtarī, “he came to be buying”: ṣāra with an imperfect marks a new, lasting habit. bi-dūni al-qīma, “for less than the value”: bi- gives the price. tuhma, “suspicion, accusation”. Here the husband's tale ends.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ فِي زَمَنِهِ عُصْفُورٌ يَأْتِي كُلَّ يَوْمٍ إِلَى مَلِكٍ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الطُّيُورِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ غَادِيًا وَرَائِحًا عِنْدَهُ بِحَيْثُ كَانَ أَوَّلَ دَاخِلٍ عَلَيْهِ وَآخِرَ خَارِجٍ مِنْ عِنْدِةِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna fī zamanihi ʿuṣfūrun yaʾtī kulla yawmin ilā malikin min mulūki al-ṭuyūri wa-lam yazal ghādiyan wa-rāʾiḥan ʿindahu bi-ḥaythu kāna awwala dākhilin ʿalayhi wa-ākhira khārijin min ʿindihi
sentences.l: And there-was in his-time a sparrow coming every day to a king of the kings of the birds; and he-did-not cease going-at-dawn and returning-at-dusk with-him, such-that he-was (the) first entering upon-him and (the) last going-out from with-him.
sentences.i: In his time there was a sparrow who came every day to one of the kings of the birds. He was forever coming and going at his court, morning and evening, so that he was the first to come in to him and the last to leave.
sentences.n: The tale moves straight on to a new fable, of a sparrow; “in his time” ties it loosely to the man of the last story. ghādiyan wa-rāʾiḥan, “going out at dawn and coming back at dusk”: constantly to and fro. bi-ḥaythu, “so that, to the point that”: bi- here introduces the result. awwal dākhil / ākhir khārij, “the first in / the last out”, is a balanced pair. عندة, with ة for the pronoun ه, is again the print's spelling.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّ جَمَاعَةً مِنَ الطُّيُورِ اجْتَمَعُوا فِي جَبَلٍ عَالٍ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa anna jamāʿatan mina al-ṭuyūri ijtamaʿū fī jabalin ʿālin mina al-jibāli
sentences.l: And it-happened that a company of the birds gathered on a mountain high of the mountains.
sentences.i: It happened that a company of birds gathered on a high mountain.
sentences.n: ijtamaʿū, a masculine plural verb for the birds: they are treated as persons, as throughout these fables.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ إِنَّا قَدْ كَثُرْنَا وَكَثُرَ الِاخْتِلَافُ بَيْنَنَا وَلَابُدَّ لَنَا مِنْ مَلِكٍ يَنْظُرُ فِي أُمُورِنَا فَتَجْتَمِعُ كَلِمَتُنَا وَيَزُولُ الِاخْتِلَافُ عَنَّا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla baʿḍuhum li-baʿḍin innā qad kathurnā wa-kathura al-ikhtilāfu baynanā wa-lā budda lanā min malikin yanẓuru fī umūrinā fa-tajtamiʿu kalimatunā wa-yazūlu al-ikhtilāfu ʿannā
sentences.l: And some-of-them said to others: We have-grown-many, and the disagreement has-grown-much between-us; and there-is-no escape for-us from a king (who) looks into our-affairs, so our-word comes-together and the disagreement passes-away from-us.
sentences.i: They said to one another, “We have grown many, and so have our quarrels; we must have a king to look after our affairs, so that we may be of one mind and our quarrels may leave us.”
sentences.n: baʿḍuhum li-baʿḍin, “some of them to others”: to one another. lā budda lanā min, “we cannot do without”. ijtamaʿat kalimatuhum, “their word came together”: they were united. ولابدّ is set as one word in the print; its shadda is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَمَرَّ بِهِمْ ذَلِكَ الْعُصْفُورُ فَأَشَارَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِتَمْلِيكِ الطَّاؤُوسِ وَهُوَ الْمَلِكُ الَّذِي يَتَرَدَّدُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-marra bihim dhālika al-ʿuṣfūru fa-ashāra ʿalayhim bi-tamlīki al-ṭāʾūsi wa-huwa al-maliku alladhī yataraddadu ilayhi
sentences.l: And that sparrow passed by-them, and he-advised them toward the making-king of the peacock; and he (was) the king whom he-goes-back-and-forth to-him.
sentences.i: That sparrow passed by them, and advised them to make the peacock king: he was the king whom the sparrow used to visit.
sentences.n: marra bi-, “to pass by”: the verb chooses bi-. ashāra ʿalā … bi-, “to advise someone to”: bi- carries what is advised. tamlīk, “making someone king”. taraddada ilā, “to go back and forth to, frequent”. الطاؤوس, “the peacock”, is printed with a hamza on a wāw seat; ṭāʾūs and ṭāwūs are both said. The shadda in فمرّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَاخْتَارُوا الطَّاؤُوسَ وَجَعَلُوهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مَلِكًا
sentences.tr: fa-ikhtārū al-ṭāʾūsa wa-jaʿalūhu ʿalayhim malikan
sentences.l: And they-chose the peacock and made-him over-them king.
sentences.i: So they chose the peacock and made him king over them.

sentences.t: فَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَجَعَلَ ذَلِكَ الْعُصْفُورَ كَاتِبَهُ وَوَزِيرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-aḥsana ilayhim wa-jaʿala dhālika al-ʿuṣfūra kātibahu wa-wazīrahu
sentences.l: And he-did-good to-them, and made that sparrow his-secretary and his-vizier.
sentences.i: He treated them well, and made the sparrow his secretary and his vizier.
sentences.n: aḥsana ilā, “to treat kindly, do good to”.

sentences.t: فَكَانَ تَارَةً يَتْرُكُ الْمُلَازَمَةَ وَيَنْظُرُ فِى الْأُمُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-kāna tāratan yatruku al-mulāzamata wa-yanẓuru fī al-umūri
sentences.l: And he-was at-times leaving the attendance and looking into the affairs.
sentences.i: At times he would leave off his close attendance and see to affairs.
sentences.n: mulāzama, “constant attendance, keeping close to someone”. Who leaves off attending is not said: most likely the sparrow, now a vizier with business of his own, which prepares for his absence in the next sentence. فى is again fī.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعُصْفُورَ غَابَ يَوْمًا عَنِ الطَّاؤُوسِ فَقَلِقَ قَلَقًا عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿuṣfūra ghāba yawman ʿani al-ṭāʾūsi fa-qaliqa qalaqan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: Then the sparrow was-absent a day from the peacock, and he-was-uneasy an unease great.
sentences.i: Then one day the sparrow stayed away from the peacock, who grew very uneasy.
sentences.n: qaliqa qalaqan ʿaẓīman, “was uneasy with a great unease”: the verb's own noun as an internal object, for emphasis.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْعُصْفُورُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa ka-dhālika idh dakhala ʿalayhi al-ʿuṣfūru
sentences.l: And while he (was) like that, lo, the sparrow came-in upon-him.
sentences.i: While he was in this state, the sparrow came in to him.
sentences.n: baynamā … idh, “while … suddenly”: the stock frame for an arrival. ka-dhālika, “like that”: ka- compares.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا الَّذِي أَخَّرَكَ وَأَنْتَ أَقْرَبُ الْأَتْبَاعِ إِلَيْنَا وَأَعَزُّهُمْ عَلَيْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu mā alladhī akhkharaka wa-anta aqrabu al-atbāʿi ilaynā wa-aʿazzuhum ʿalaynā
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: What (is) it-that delayed-you, and you (are) the nearest of the followers to-us and the dearest-of-them to-us?
sentences.i: The peacock said to him, “What kept you, when you are the closest of our followers to us and the dearest of them to us?”
sentences.n: wa-anta …, “while you are …”: a circumstantial clause opened by wa-. aʿazz ʿalā, “dearer to”. The rhyme ilaynā / ʿalaynā closes the question. The shaddas in اخّرك and واعزّهم are the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعُصْفُورُ رَأَيْتُ أَمْرًا وَاشْتَبَهَ عَلَيَّ فَتَخَوَّفْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿuṣfūru raʾaytu amran wa-ishtabaha ʿalayya fa-takhawwaftu minhu
sentences.l: And the sparrow said: I-saw a thing, and it-was-obscure to-me, so I-grew-afraid of-it.
sentences.i: The sparrow said, “I saw something I could not make out, and it frightened me.”
sentences.n: ishtabaha ʿalā, “to be unclear, doubtful to someone”. The shadda in عليّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الطَّاوُوسُ مَا الَّذِى رَأَيْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ṭāwūsu mā alladhī raʾayta
sentences.l: And the peacock said to-him: What (is) it that you-saw?
sentences.i: The peacock said to him, “What did you see?”
sentences.n: Here the print spells the peacock الطاوُوس, ṭāwūs, with a wāw where it had a hamza seat before; the ḍamma is the print's own. الذى writes ى for ي.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْعُصْفُورُ رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا مَعَهُ شَبَكَةٌ قَدْ نَصَبَهَا عِنْدَ وَكْرِي وَثَبَّتَ أَوْتَادَهَا وَبَذَرَ فِي وَسَطِهَا حَبًّا وَقَعَدَ بَعِيدًا عَنْهَا
sentences.tr: qāla al-ʿuṣfūru raʾaytu rajulan maʿahu shabakatun qad naṣabahā ʿinda wakrī wa-thabbata awtādahā wa-badhara fī wasaṭihā ḥabban wa-qaʿada baʿīdan ʿanhā
sentences.l: The sparrow said: I-saw a man, with-him a net; he-had set-it-up by my-nest, and made-fast its-pegs, and scattered in its-middle grain, and sat far from-it.
sentences.i: The sparrow said, “I saw a man with a net. He had set it up by my nest and driven its pegs in firmly, scattered grain in the middle of it, and sat down some way off.
sentences.n: naṣaba, “to set up, pitch” (a net, a trap). wakr, “a bird's nest”. thabbata, “to make fast”. ḥabb, “grain, seed”. The shadda in حبّا is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسْتُ أَنْظُرُ مَا يَفْعَلُ
sentences.tr: fa-jalastu anẓuru mā yafʿalu
sentences.l: So I-sat watching what he-does.
sentences.i: So I sat and watched to see what he would do.
sentences.n: anẓuru, “watching”: an imperfect describing what he did as he sat.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِكُرْكِيٍّ هُوَ وَزَوْجَتُهُ قَدْ سَاقَهُمَا الْقَضَاءُ وَالْقَدَرُ حَتَّى سَقَطَا فِي وَسَطِ الشَّبَكَةِ وَصَارَا يَصْرُخَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-kurkiyyin huwa wa-zawjatuhu qad sāqahumā al-qaḍāʾu wa-al-qadaru ḥattā saqaṭā fī wasaṭi al-shabakati wa-ṣārā yaṣrukhāni
sentences.l: And while I (was) thus, and behold, a crane, he and his wife: the decree and the destiny had driven-them, until they-two fell in the middle of the net, and they-two began crying-out.
sentences.i: And while I sat so, a crane came, he and his mate, driven by fate and destiny, until the two of them dropped into the middle of the net and set up a shrieking.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-…, “and behold …”: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears. kurkī, “crane”. al-qaḍāʾ wa-al-qadar, “the decree and the destiny”, the stock pair for what God has fixed; the rhyme is in the pair itself. ṣārā yaṣrukhāni, “they became crying”: ṣāra with a following present verb means “to begin to”, a construction the Nights uses constantly.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الصَّيَّادُ وَأَخَذَهُمَا فَأَزْعَجَنِي ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-ṣayyādu wa-akhadhahumā fa-azʿajanī dhālika
sentences.l: And the fowler rose and took-them-two, and that alarmed-me.
sentences.i: The fowler got up and took them both, and that frightened me.
sentences.n: ṣayyād, “hunter”, here a fowler, a catcher of birds. azʿaja, “to disturb, alarm”.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا سَبَبُ غِيَابِي عَنْكَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ وَمَا بَقِيتُ أَسْكُنُ هَذَا الْوَكْرَ حَذَرًا مِنَ الشَّبَكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā sababu ghiyābī ʿanka yā malika al-zamāni wa-mā baqītu askunu hādhā al-wakra ḥadharan mina al-shabakati
sentences.l: And this (is the) cause of my-absence from-you, O king of the time; and I-no-longer dwell (in) this nest, out-of-caution from the net.”
sentences.i: That is why I have been away from you, O king of the age; and I no longer live in this nest, for fear of the net.”
sentences.n: mā baqītu askunu, “I did not remain dwelling”, i.e. “I no longer live”: mā baqiya with a present verb is “no longer to do”. wakr, a bird's nest. ḥadharan, “out of caution”, a verbal noun in the accusative giving the reason (mafʿūl li-ajlihi). yā malika al-zamān, “O king of the age”, the sparrow's address to the peacock, king of the birds.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الطَّاؤُوسُ لَا تَرْحَلْ مِنْ مَكَانِكَ فَلَا يَنْفَعُكَ الْحَذَرُ مِنَ الْقَدَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ṭāʾūsu lā tarḥal min makānika fa-lā yanfaʿuka al-ḥadharu mina al-qadari
sentences.l: And the peacock said to-him: Do-not depart from your-place, for the caution will-not profit-you against the destiny.
sentences.i: The peacock said to him, “Do not leave your place: caution will not save you from fate.”
sentences.n: ḥadhar and qadar rhyme: the peacock's answer is a proverb in little, al-ḥadhar lā yanfaʿ min al-qadar, “caution is no use against destiny”. The print spells ṭāʾūs with a hamza seat and a second wāw, الطاؤوس.

sentences.t: فَامْتَثَلَ أَمْرَهُ وَقَالَ سَأَصْبِرُ وَلَا أَرْحَلُ طَاعَةً لِلْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-imtathala amrahu wa-qāla sa-aṣbiru wa-lā arḥalu ṭāʿatan li-al-maliki
sentences.l: And he-complied-with his-command and said: I-will-be-patient and not depart, (in) obedience to-the-king.
sentences.i: The sparrow did as he was told, saying, “I will bear it and not leave, in obedience to the king.”
sentences.n: imtathala amrahu, “he conformed to his order”, the usual phrase for obeying a command. ṭāʿatan, “in obedience”, accusative of reason again.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْعُصْفُورُ حَذِرًا عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَأَخَذَ الطَّعَامَ إِلَى الطَّاؤُوسِ فَأَكَلَ حَتَّى اكْتَفَى وَتَنَاوَلَ عَلَى الطَّعَامِ الْمَاءَ وَذَهَبَ الْعُصْفُورُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-ʿuṣfūru ḥadhiran ʿalā nafsihi wa-akhadha al-ṭaʿāma ilā al-ṭāʾūsi fa-akala ḥattā iktafā wa-tanāwala ʿalā al-ṭaʿāmi al-māʾa wa-dhahaba al-ʿuṣfūru
sentences.l: And the sparrow did-not cease (being) wary for himself; and he-took the food to the peacock, and he-ate until he-had-enough, and took upon the food the water; and the sparrow went (off).
sentences.i: Yet the sparrow stayed on his guard. He brought the peacock his food, and the peacock ate his fill and drank water after it, and the sparrow went his way.
sentences.n: lam yazal, “did not cease”, with a predicate in the accusative: “remained”. ḥadhiran ʿalā nafsihi, “wary for himself”; ḥadhir is the adjective, where the previous sentences had the noun ḥadhar. The subject of fa-akala is left to the sense: the sparrow takes the food, the peacock eats it. tanāwala ʿalā al-ṭaʿāmi al-māʾa, “took the water upon the food”, that is, drank after eating.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ شَاخِصٌ وَإِذَا بِعُصْفُورَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ فِى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa fī baʿḍi al-ayyāmi shākhiṣun wa-idhā bi-ʿuṣfūrayni yaqtatilāni fī al-arḍi
sentences.l: And while he (was) on one of the days gazing, and behold, two sparrows fighting-each-other on the ground.
sentences.i: One day, as he sat looking about him, he saw two sparrows fighting on the ground.
sentences.n: shākhiṣ, “staring, gazing fixedly” (active participle of shakhaṣa), the predicate of huwa. yaqtatilāni, form VIII of qatala, “to fight one another”. The print writes fī here with ى, فى, as it often does.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ كَيْفَ أَكُونُ وَزِيرَ الْمَلِكِ وَأَرَى الْعَصَافِيرَ تَقْتَتِلُ فِي جِوَارِى وَاللَّهِ لَأُصْلِحَنَّ بَيْنَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi kayfa akūnu wazīra al-maliki wa-arā al-ʿaṣāfīra taqtatilu fī jiwārī wa-Allāhi la-uṣliḥanna baynahumā
sentences.l: And he said in himself: How (can) I-be the vizier of the king and see the sparrows fight-each-other in my-neighbourhood? By-God, I-will-surely-make-peace between-them-two!
sentences.i: He said to himself, “How can I be the king's vizier and watch sparrows fighting next door to me? By God, I will make peace between them!”
sentences.n: The sparrow is the peacock's vizier. jiwār, “neighbourhood, vicinity”: fī jiwārī, “near me”; the print writes the final -ī with ى. la-uṣliḥanna, “I shall surely reconcile”: la- of the oath with the energetic -anna, after wa-Allāhi. The hamza on وأرى is printed in the edition.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَيْهِمَا لِيُصْلِحَ بَيْنَهُمَا فَقَلَبَ الصَّيَّادُ الشَّبَكَةَ عَلَي الْجَمِيعِ فَوَقَعَ ذَلِكَ الْعُصْفُورُ فِي وَسَطِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma dhahaba ilayhimā li-yuṣliḥa baynahumā fa-qalaba al-ṣayyādu al-shabakata ʿalā al-jamīʿi fa-waqaʿa dhālika al-ʿuṣfūru fī wasaṭihā
sentences.l: Then he went to-them-two to make-peace between-them-two; and the fowler turned the net over all (of them), and that sparrow fell in its-middle.
sentences.i: Then he went over to make peace between them, and the fowler threw the net over them all, and that sparrow fell into the middle of it.
sentences.n: qalaba al-shabakata, “he turned the net over”, sprang the trap. The print writes ʿalā as علي, with ي for the final ى; it is read ʿalā.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ الصَّيَّادُ وَأَخَذَةُ وَدَفَعَهُ إِلَى صَاحِبِهِ وَقٰلَ لَهُ اسْتَوْثِقْ بِهِ فَإِنَّهُ سَمِينٌ وَلَمْ أَرَ أَحْسَنَ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma ilayhi al-ṣayyādu wa-akhadhahu wa-dafaʿahu ilā ṣāḥibihi wa-qāla lahu istawthiq bihi fa-innahu samīnun wa-lam ara aḥsana minhu
sentences.l: And the fowler rose to-him and took-him and handed-him to his-companion, and said to-him: Make-sure of-him, for he (is) fat, and I-have-not seen better than-him.
sentences.i: The fowler went up to him and took him and handed him to his companion, saying, “Keep a tight hold of this one: he is fat, and I have never seen a finer.”
sentences.n: The print spells akhadhahu “he took him” as اخذة, with ة for the pronoun ـه, and qāla defectively as قل, pointed here with the dagger alif. istawthiq bihi, “make sure of him”: form X of wathiqa, with bi- naming what one makes fast. lam ara, “I have not seen”: the jussive of raʾā after lam, its final letter dropped.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعُصْفُورُ فِي نَفْسِهِ قَدْ وَقَعْتُ فِيمَا كُنْتُ أَخَافُ مِنْهُ وَمَا كَانَ أَمْنِي إِلَّا الطَّاؤُوسَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿuṣfūru fī nafsihi qad waqaʿtu fīmā kuntu akhāfu minhu wa-mā kāna amnī illā al-ṭāʾūsa
sentences.l: And the sparrow said in himself: I-have-fallen into what I-was fearing of-it; and my-safety was not but the peacock.
sentences.i: And the sparrow said to himself, “I have fallen into the very thing I feared, and all my safety lay in the peacock.
sentences.n: fīmā, “into that which”. mā kāna amnī illā al-ṭāʾūsa, literally “my security was nothing but the peacock”: his feeling of safety rested on the peacock alone, who had told him to stay. The phrase is compressed and the reading is not certain.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَنْفَعْنِى الْحَذَرُ مِنْ نُزُولِ الْقَدَرِ فَلَا مَفَرَّ مِنَ الْقَضَاءِ لِلْمُحَاذِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yanfaʿnī al-ḥadharu min nuzūli al-qadari fa-lā mafarra mina al-qaḍāʾi li-al-muḥādhiri
sentences.l: And the caution did-not profit-me against the descent of the destiny; so there-is-no escape from the decree for-the-wary-one.
sentences.i: My caution was no use to me when destiny came down; there is no escaping the decree, however wary one is.
sentences.n: ḥadhar and qadar rhyme again, and the second clause closes on muḥādhir, “the wary one”, from the same root as ḥadhar: the sparrow ends by turning the peacock's proverb on himself. lā mafarra, “there is no escape”: lā of absolute negation with its noun in the accusative, without tanwīn. The print again writes the final -ī of yanfaʿnī with ى.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And how fine (is) the saying of the poet!
sentences.i: How well the poet put it:
sentences.n: mā aḥsana …, “how fine is …!”, the exclamatory form, with its object in the accusative.

sentences.t:
مَا لَا يَكُوْنُ فَلَا يَكُوْنُ بِحِيْلَةٍ * اَبَدًا وَمَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ فَيَكُوْنُ
سَيَكُوْنُ مَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ فِي وَقْتِهِ * وَاَخُ الْجَهَالَةِ دَائِمًا مَغْبُوْنُ
sentences.tr:
mā lā yakūnu fa-lā yakūnu bi-ḥīlatin * abadan wa-mā huwa kāʾinun fa-yakūnu
sa-yakūnu mā huwa kāʾinun fī waqtihi * wa-akhu al-jahālati dāʾiman maghbūnu
sentences.l:
What will-not be, then it-will-not be by a stratagem * ever; and what is to-be, then it-will-be.
It-will-be, what is to-be, in its-time * and the brother of the ignorance (is) always cheated.
sentences.i:
What is not to be will never come about by any cunning, and what is to be will be.
What is to be will be, in its own time; and the fool is forever the loser.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own, kept as printed, including the sukūn on the long ū (يَكُوْنُ) and the bare alif of اَبَدًا and اَخُ, where the edition marks no hamza. kāʾin, “being, coming to be”, the active participle of kāna: “what is to be”. akh al-jahāla, “the brother of ignorance”, the ignorant man. The print gives اَخُ with no wāw, where Classical prose writes the construct akhū; spoken before al- the vowel is short either way (akhu l-jahālati), so the metre (kāmil) is unaffected. maghbūn, “cheated, the loser in a bargain”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ يَا شَهْرَزَادُ زِيدِينِي مِنْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku yā Shahrazādu zīdīnī min hādhā al-ḥadīthi
sentences.l: And the king said: O Shahrazād, add-for-me of this story!
sentences.i: The king said, “Shahrazād, tell me more of this story.”
sentences.n: zīdīnī, “give me more”, the feminine imperative of zāda with the suffix -nī. The king asks for more; the night ends before she can begin.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ فِى اللَّيْلَةِ الْقَابِلَةِ إِنْ أَبْقَانِي الْمَلِكُ أَعَزَّهُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat fī al-laylati al-qābilati in abqānī al-maliku aʿazzahu Allāhu
sentences.l: And she said: In the coming night, if the king lets-me-remain, may-God-make-him-mighty.
sentences.i: She said, “Tomorrow night, if the king spares me, may God give him strength.”
sentences.n: in abqānī al-malik, “if the king lets me live on”, Shahrazād's standing condition. aʿazzahu Allāh, “may God strengthen him”: a past verb used as a wish, the usual courtesy after naming a ruler.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
